items.title: Quasi-compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed, and disjoint quasi-compact subsets can be separated by open sets
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file topology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the standard compactness-separation lemma in a Hausdorff space (author lemma at source lines 1893-1901, label lemma-quasi-compact-in-Hausdorff): quasi-compact subsets are closed, and two disjoint quasi-compact subsets have disjoint open neighbourhoods. The proof (source lines 1903-1920) is the classical double compactness argument, written out in full: the first part separates a point from a quasi-compact set by finitely many neighbourhoods (proof lines 1904-1910), and the second part iterates the first over the points of one of the two subsets and then takes a finite intersection on the other side (proof lines 1910-1919). The lemma is used throughout the chapter when separatedness of quasi-compact pieces is needed. H2.
